instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor. This step is part of prep, but crucial for flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Sauce Flavor
instructions.text: Stir in 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1 teaspoon ground coriander, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until aromatic. Pour in the crushed tomatoes or tomato puree. Add the drained soaked cashews and 1/2 cup water. Bring to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Simmer and Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Reduce heat to low, cover, and let the sauce simmer for 10-12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to do this in batches.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the blended sauce to the pan. Add the cooked chicken, sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste). Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly. Crush the kasoori methi between your palms and stir it into the butter chicken. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

article:
Discover the Magic of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Indian Lunch Recipe

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian curry has transcended borders, becoming a beloved staple in homes and restaurants worldwide. Its rich, creamy, and subtly sweet tomato-based sauce, enveloping tender pieces of marinated chicken, offers an unparalleled culinary experience. Perfect for a hearty lunch, a comforting dinner, or a special occasion, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani promises a symphony of flavors that will leave you craving more. If you've ever dreamt of recreating this restaurant-quality dish in your own kitchen, you've come to the right place. Get ready to embark on a delicious journey that will demystify this classic and empower you to cook an authentic Murgh Makhani that tastes like it’s straight from a Delhi dhaba.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in the 1950s in Delhi, India, it's a dish born from resourcefulness at the Moti Mahal restaurant. Legend has it that chefs combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato gravy, cream, and butter to prevent it from drying out. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained immense popularity. What makes Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani so distinct is its luxurious texture and balanced flavor profile. Unlike many fiery Indian curries, Murgh Makhani offers a milder, sweeter, and tangier taste, making it incredibly approachable for all palates. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and spices before being cooked, often grilled or pan-fried, and then simmered in a velvety sauce made from tomatoes, ginger, garlic, cashews, and a generous amount of butter and cream. It’s a celebration of comfort food, embodying warmth and indulgence in every spoonful.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani requires a few key components, divided into the chicken marinade and the rich makhani sauce. Don't be intimidated by the list; many are common pantry staples.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500-700g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breast), cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (plus more for finishing)
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes (or 2 tablespoons almond flour)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1/4 cup heavy cream (plus more for garnish)
*   1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making delicious Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani at home is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a foolproof result:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine all ingredients for the chicken marinade. Add the chicken pieces, ensuring they are thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Build the Makhani Sauce:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or tomato puree), soaked cashews (drained), red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, sugar, and salt. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down.
5.  **Blend for Smoothness:** Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  **Simmer and Finish:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces. Stir in the heavy cream and the crushed kasuri methi. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed. Finish with an extra knob of butter for extra richness.
7.  **Garnish and Serve:** Ladle the hot Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of extra cream, if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

To elevate your homemade Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani from good to absolutely outstanding, keep these professional tips in mind:

*   **Quality Ingredients Matter:** Use good quality, ripe tomatoes or a reputable brand of crushed tomatoes. Fresh ginger-garlic paste makes a noticeable difference. Don't skimp on the butter and cream – they are essential for the signature richness.
*   **Marination is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination in the refrigerator is highly recommended.
*   **Char the Chicken:** If you have an oven with a broiler or a grill, giving your marinated chicken pieces a quick char before adding them to the sauce will infuse a delicious smoky depth, mimicking the tandoor oven effect. Pan-frying until well-browned is a good alternative.
*   **Smooth Sauce is Paramount:** Blending the sauce thoroughly until it’s silky smooth is crucial. If you don't have a high-powered blender, passing the sauce through a sieve will remove any lingering bits of onion or cashews, ensuring that restaurant-quality texture.
*   **Low and Slow Simmer:** After adding the chicken and cream, allow the Butter Chicken to simmer gently for at least 10-15 minutes. This gives the chicken time to absorb the flavors of the makhani sauce and allows the spices to bloom fully.
*   **Don't Skip Kasuri Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) are non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani. Gently crush them between your palms before adding to release their unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan, especially garlic naan or butter naan, is the ultimate vehicle for soaking up every last drop of the rich sauce. Its soft texture and slightly chewy bite complement the creamy curry perfectly.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice, with its fragrant aroma and long grains, provides a comforting base. A simple jeera rice (cumin rice) also pairs wonderfully, adding another layer of subtle spice.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita (yogurt with grated cucumber and spices) offers a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad of sliced onions, cucumbers, and tomatoes dressed with lemon juice and a pinch of salt can provide a fresh, crunchy counterpoint.
*   **Pickles & Chutneys:** A small dollop of your favorite Indian pickle or mango chutney can add a delightful burst of flavor and acidity.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, you can easily adapt it to suit different dietary needs or taste preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace the chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas. Marinate paneer or tofu similarly to the chicken (minus the yogurt if using tofu, just spices) and pan-fry before adding to the sauce.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** For a dairy-free version, use coconut yogurt for the marinade, coconut oil instead of butter, and full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of heavy cream. Ensure to use a dairy-free butter alternative for finishing.
*   **Spice Level:** To increase the heat, add more red chili powder to the sauce, or include a finely chopped green chili during the onion sautéing step. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews from the sauce. While they contribute to the richness, the sauce will still be delicious. Alternatively, use 1-2 tablespoons of poppy seeds or sunflower seeds, soaked and blended, for a similar thickening effect.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A quick trick for a smoky flavor without a tandoor is to place a small piece of burning charcoal in a small heatproof bowl inside the pot of finished curry. Drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over the charcoal, cover immediately, and let it infuse for 5-10 minutes.

With these instructions and tips, you're well on your way to mastering the art of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani. This delightful Indian lunch recipe is more than just a meal; it's an experience that brings warmth and joy to any table. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to impress yourself and your loved ones with this truly magnificent dish. Enjoy the rich, creamy goodness!
